title: Metrics comparison view: baseline vs canary cohorts (latency, errors, tokens/sec)
creator: Tessa Morgan
description:
Goal
Design the customer-facing metrics comparison experience for Hosted canary rollouts so users can quickly answer: “Is the canary worse than baseline?” and “Should I proceed, pause, or rollback?”

This ticket covers:
- Layout and interaction model for cohort comparison charts and summary stats.
- Guidance text and warning states to prevent misinterpretation (small sample sizes, regional skew, step transitions).
- Alignment with stop-conditions/guardrails (auto-pause/rollback signals surfaced clearly, without claiming statistical rigor we don’t have).

Non-goals (for GA scope)
- Fully automated quality gates / eval-driven promotion decisions.
- Advanced statistical testing UI (p-values, confidence intervals). We can add later if telemetry supports.
- Dedicated/Private parity (ensure layout is extensible and terminology is consistent).

Primary user stories
1) As a developer, while a rollout is running, I can compare baseline vs canary on latency and errors to decide whether to continue.
2) As an admin/approver, I can validate that canary impact is acceptable across regions and time windows before approving the next step.
3) As an on-call engineer (customer-side), I can quickly spot whether a regression is concentrated in a region/model version and rollback.

Design principles
- Fast read: summary first, details on demand.
- “Explain the data”: call out what the metrics include/exclude, and when the view may be misleading.
- Avoid false precision: show rates and deltas with contextual caveats (sample size, window, step change markers).
- Cohort clarity: baseline and canary must be visually distinct, consistent across all charts, and never swapped.

Proposed information architecture (Rollout details → Metrics tab)
A) Header + context row
- Rollout name + route + environment (Hosted)
- Current step and traffic split (e.g., “Step 3: 25% canary”) + state (Running/Paused/Auto-paused)
- Time window selector (default: “Last 30 min” for running rollouts; “Last 24h” for completed)
- Filters: Region (All / per region), Model version (fixed by rollout but show baseline/canary identifiers), Request type (chat/embeddings where applicable), Status codes (All / errors only)

B) “At a glance” comparison cards (top row)
- Error rate (5xx + timeouts) with baseline value, canary value, absolute delta and relative delta
- p95 latency with baseline value, canary value, delta
- Throughput proxy: tokens/sec (or “output tokens/sec” if that’s what telemetry supports) with delta
- (Optional for GA if ready): cancel rate / client disconnect rate (especially for streaming)

Card behaviors:
- Each card includes a mini sparkline for baseline and canary over the selected window.
- Cards include a “Data quality” subline: “n=12.4k requests” (and/or “n=3.1M tokens”) + last updated timestamp.
- If n is below threshold (TBD with SRE/Telemetry), display a “Low volume” warning and de-emphasize delta (gray text, tooltips).

C) Trend charts (core)
Three primary time series charts, stacked:
1) Latency (p50 + p95)
   - Toggle: p50 / p95 / both
   - Two lines: baseline (blue) and canary (purple)
   - Step-change markers: vertical markers at step transitions, labeled with new split percentage (e.g., “→ 25%”).
   - Tooltip includes: value, sample count, region (if filtered), and whether auto-stop evaluation is using that metric.

2) Error rate
   - Metric definition: (5xx + timeouts) / total requests. Include hover help with exact status codes included.
   - If user filters “errors only,” show error counts + breakdown by 429/5xx/timeout rather than rate (avoid 100% confusion).

3) Tokens/sec (or output tokens/sec)
   - Clarify: This is aggregate throughput for the selected filters, not per-request speed.
   - Useful to detect batching/queueing changes, capacity constraints, and canary performance regressions.

D) Breakdown table (below charts)
Purpose: quickly localize regressions.
- Default grouping: Region
- Alternate groupings (dropdown): Model region, AZ (if exposed), or “Error class” (timeout vs 5xx vs 429)
- Columns:
  - Baseline: error rate, p95 latency, tokens/sec, request count
  - Canary: same
  - Delta: absolute + %
  - “Flags”: low volume, missing data, “auto-stop triggered” (if applicable)
- Table rows sortable by worst delta.

E) Guidance and interpretation (right rail or expandable section)
A short “How to read this” section:
- “Look for consistent changes over at least one soak window.”
- “Compare by region: a regression in one region may indicate capacity or routing imbalance.”
- “Low request volume can make deltas noisy; consider extending the window.”
- “If streaming: client disconnects can affect observed tokens/sec and latency.”

When auto-pause/rollback occurs, show a prominent callout:
- “Rollout paused automatically due to SLO breach”
- Metric that triggered (e.g., canary p95 latency +35% vs baseline for 10 min) + threshold summary
- Link: “View stop condition details” (ties to orchestrator events / DES-755 timeline panel)

Copy + terminology notes
- Use “Baseline” and “Canary” consistently; avoid “control/treatment” in GA UI.
- Use “p95 latency” (not “95th percentile”) in the main UI; expand in tooltip.
- Use “Timeouts” explicitly (customers care) and include in error rate definition.
- Avoid implying causality: use “observed” / “measured” rather than “caused by canary.”

Edge cases to handle
1) Cohort tagging delays / missing data
- If canary line is missing: show empty state: “No canary traffic observed in this window.”
- If baseline present but canary absent at low splits: suggest increasing window or waiting for traffic.

2) Step transitions
- During split changes, metrics will shift; markers should help users avoid misreading short spikes.
- Consider a small “cooldown” note: “Metrics may fluctuate for 1–2 minutes after a step change.” (confirm with SRE)

3) Region skew
- When “All regions” is selected, add a footnote: “Aggregated across regions; regional spikes may be masked.”
- Encourage using the breakdown table.

4) Low volume
- Define a UI threshold (proposal):
  - “Low volume” warning if canary requests < 500 in window OR canary tokens < 250k.
  - “Insufficient data” if canary requests < 50.
- Thresholds must be confirmed with Logan/Aisha based on telemetry characteristics.

5) Misleading tokens/sec
- If customers run different prompt sizes between cohorts (shouldn’t happen with deterministic cohorting, but can happen with client retries or multi-route confusion), tokens/sec may shift. Add tooltip: “Differences in request mix can affect tokens/sec.”

Open questions
- Metric naming: do we have “tokens/sec” as a stable exposed metric, or do we need to label as “Output tokens/sec” / “Generated tokens/sec”?
- Do we have enough telemetry to compute percent-change vs baseline reliably at low splits without huge variance?
- Can we annotate the chart with auto-stop evaluation windows (e.g., shaded intervals) or just show the event marker?
- What’s the default time window for running rollouts (30m vs 60m) given typical soak times?

Design artifacts
- Figma: “Hosted Rollouts – Metrics Compare” (Page: Rollout details)
- Components used: Console chart primitives (line chart with dual series), metrics cards, warning callouts.
- Interaction spec includes: tooltips, empty states, low-volume warnings, and step-marker annotations.

Implementation notes (for Eng)
- Charts must support two series (baseline/canary) and be resilient to sparse canary data.
- Provide a stable color mapping across Console (baseline blue, canary purple) with sufficient contrast and colorblind-safe patterns (dash style optional).
- Table sort must not reorder the ‘All regions’ row (keep pinned).
- Performance: avoid rendering too many datapoints (server-side downsampling or client bucketing).

Acceptance criteria
- A customer can select a time window and compare baseline vs canary for error rate, p50/p95 latency, and tokens/sec.
- Step transitions are visible and help explain changes.
- The UI clearly warns about low volume / insufficient data.
- The view cleanly integrates with the rollout timeline/audit panel for auto-pause/rollback events (links or embedded callouts).
- Copy is finalized for GA (approved by Design + PM; reviewed for consistency with docs).

Next steps
- Final review with Dylan/Felix on feasibility of card+chart layout and table groupings.
- Confirm thresholds and definitions with Logan/Aisha (Telemetry/SRE).
- Align with Wei/Elliot on doc wording and screenshots for GA docs PR.
comments: 2025-01-22 (Tessa Morgan): Creating this ticket to lock the metrics compare view before we finalize the wizard + rollout details IA. Key risk: users misreading noisy canary metrics at 1% traffic; we need strong guidance + low-volume states.

2025-01-29 (Kenji Nakamura): Drafted v1 layout: top summary cards + three charts + breakdown table. Added step markers. Pending confirmation from Telemetry on tokens/sec definition and whether we can show p50+p95 in one chart without clutter.

2025-02-03 (Felix Schneider): From implementation POV: dual-series charts OK; step markers doable if backend returns step-change events with timestamps. Table grouping by region is straightforward; adding AZ grouping might require exposing infra metadata (probably not GA).

2025-02-07 (Paula Mendes): Please ensure the stop-condition trigger shows clearly as “paused automatically” and references the metric/threshold. We should not require users to hunt in the timeline to understand why it paused.

2025-02-12 (Aisha Bello): Strongly recommend default window = last 60 minutes during beta. At 1–5% splits many routes won’t hit stable p95 deltas in 30 min. Also +1 to showing request counts prominently; otherwise we’ll get false positives in support.

2025-02-18 (Logan Wright): Telemetry can provide request_count and token_count for both cohorts, plus p50/p95 latency and error_rate. Tokens/sec will be derived and may be labelled “Generated tokens/sec” (output tokens). We can bucket per-minute to keep charts lightweight.
2025-03-04 (Kenji Nakamura): Updated copy: replaced “statistically significant” language with “consistent over time.” Added low-volume thresholds placeholders; need final numbers from SRE.

2025-03-12 (Wei Chen): For docs/screenshot consistency, please keep terminology aligned with PRD: “Baseline” and “Canary”, and “Step” for split changes. Also please add a small inline definition for error rate (5xx + timeouts).
2025-03-21 (Tessa Morgan): Marking In Review for final sign-off. Remaining: confirm low-volume thresholds + finalize tokens/sec label. Otherwise ready to hand off.
